key_insight: A PINN-trained, solver-agnostic turbulence-closure framework learns generalizable RANS closures across multiple bluff-body wakes without embedding a CFD solver in the training loop.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster screening of closure forms and more portable turbulence models that can be trained on diverse data and then deployed in conventional finite-element solvers.
method: Train closures by enforcing the RANS residual with automatic differentiation inside a PINN.
Compare four closure families: local stress, non-local stress with turbulent kinetic energy transport, learned-length-scale stress, and direct Reynolds-force modeling.
Improve coupled stability with input-gradient smoothing and a Lipschitz constraint before freezing the learned closure for deployment.
evidence_signal: The models were trained on six 2D bluff-body wakes at Re = 10^4 and evaluated with in-sample tests plus strict leave-one-shape-out validation, where the force model achieved the best out-of-sample mean-velocity and drag performance (about 8.5% LOSO drag error).
watch_item: Generalization and stability still depend on the training distribution and on careful enforcement of solver robustness when the learned closure is coupled back into a CFD solver.
paper_title: Generalizable turbulence closures across bluff-body shapes by PINN-based solver-agnostic training
